turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, nice to meet you too, but I didn't exactly drive myself here today. They brought me in. My family, the fair organizers, the whole lot of them made a massive fuss out of nothing, really, but they insisted. 

See, we were down at the county fair, and I was giving my talk—I usually do a little presentation on equipment management and soil turnover, you know, for the younger guys coming up in the business. I've been running my farm for forty years, so I know a thing or two. But right in the middle of my speech, I just... I realized words weren't going to cut it. I had to show them. So I climbed right up onto the big display tractor they had parked by the stage. Just scrambled right up there into the cab right in the middle of my talk! 

And I grabbed hold of the levers and I kept jerking the controls, just yanking them back and forth, because I needed to show the crowd the new pattern. It’s a very specific pattern, you see, a 'new pattern' for how the machinery is supposed to move with the earth, and I was jerking the gears around to demonstrate exactly how it flows. And the thing was... I couldn't make myself stop. I just couldn't. It was like I was locked in. People were yelling at me, screaming from the front rows, the fair manager was hollering for me to get down, waving his arms around like a madman, but my hands just kept going. I couldn't stop jerking those levers and showing them the pattern, even with everybody yelling their heads off at me. 

Eventually they had to climb up and physically pull me off the machine. And then they dragged me straight over here. So... that's what brings me in.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes climbing onto a display tractor during a speech and uncontrollably jerking the controls to demonstrate a 'new pattern,' unable to stop despite people yelling, which is a clear example of severely disturbed, inappropriate, and disorganized motor behavior.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually high or overly energized lately?
turns.patient_response:
Well, you know, it’s funny you put it that way, because... well, yes and no. It’s not just a simple "high," it’s more like... it’s like the whole world is just humming, you know? Some mornings I wake up before the sun even thinks about rising, and I step out onto the porch, and I swear to you, it feels like the entire valley is just opening up specifically for me. Like the land itself is waiting on my command. And I’ll just stand out there grinning at absolutely nothing, feeling this incredible surge of power, like I could plow a hundred acres by hand before breakfast. It’s a magnificent feeling, really. 

But the thing is, it doesn't take much to ruin it. It's like walking a tightrope. If I’m out there feeling like a king, and one of the hired hands—say, Jimmy, he’s been with us three years but still doesn't know how to properly grease a combine—if he questions an order I give, or even just looks at me sideways... or if my wife, Mary, comes out and tells me I need to slow down, that I'm talking too fast or doing too much... well, I just lose it. I snap. And I don't just get annoyed, I get furious. I lash out like they've just insulted the family name, like they've spat on my grandfather's grave. The anger just bubbles up so fast and so hot, I can't even control what comes out of my mouth. One minute I'm on top of the world, and the next I'm ready to tear somebody's head off just for telling me to take a breath. So, energized? Yes. But it’s a sharp kind of energy, you know? It cuts.

The whole morning, the whole afternoon, I'm just riding this wave where everything feels grand and I'm on top of it all.

turns.doctor_question: Have you felt that you have special powers or a special mission that other people do not have?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it’s not so much a "power" like in a comic book, but... yes, a mission, absolutely. See, I’ve been working this land for forty years, and you get to know the dirt. You get to know how it breathes. And lately, it’s become clear as day to me—crystal clear—that I am the one farmer in this entire county, maybe the whole state, who actually understands what needs to be done. I’ve figured out this entirely new way of growing, a whole new system of crop rotation and soil turnover that works with the natural magnetic pull of the earth. 

I’ve been trying to explain it to people. I sat down and drew up these charts—beautiful, detailed charts showing the yield projections—and I took them down to the university extension office. And you know what they did? Those kids in their clean button-down shirts, who probably couldn't tell a soybean from a pinto bean if it bit them, they just smiled at me. Patted me on the head, practically. And the lenders at the bank, same thing. I went in to get a loan to overhaul the combines for this new method, and they looked at me like I was speaking Greek. 

But I know I'm right. I feel it in my bones. I am absolutely sure I can prove this new way of growing, and those university people and the bankers, they ought to be sitting down and taking notes from me instead of doubting me and looking at their watches. They should be begging me for the secret! Because once I get the machinery moving in that new pattern—like I was trying to show them at the fair—it’s going to revolutionize agriculture. I just need them to stop getting in my way and listen for five minutes, because I’m the only one who sees the big picture here. The only one.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient exhibits extreme grandiosity, believing he is the only person who understands this new system and that experts should be begging him for his secret.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it’s... you see, that’s another thing entirely. Now, I don't know about seeing things, my eyes are as good as they were when I was twenty, but hearing... well, yes. But it’s not just random noise, Doc. It's very specific, and it's important. 

You know my north pasture? The one that slopes down toward the old creek bed? We put in a new set of irrigation lines down there about, oh, must be five years ago now. Good quality aluminum. Anyway, lately... especially right around dusk, when the sun is just dipping behind the ridge and the light gets all long and orange, and the wind dies down so it's just dead quiet out there... I’ll go out to check the valves. And I hear them. Voices. Clear as a bell, coming right out of the metal of those irrigation lines. 

At first, I thought maybe it was just the water pressure whistling, you know how pipes do, or maybe the metal catching a radio frequency somehow. But no, it’s voices. Real, distinct voices. And they’re talking to me about the dirt, about the crops. They tell me exactly which rows are blessed—which ones are going to yield up strong and pure—and which rows are poisoned. Just straight up poisoned from the roots. And I have to listen, because if I don't mark off the poisoned rows, the whole harvest could be compromised. 

And the strange thing is, Mary thinks it's just because I've been working too hard, or because I've been running hot with all that energy I was telling you about earlier. She thinks I'm just overtired and wound up. But I've been keeping track, Doc. I hear those voices in the pipes even on the weeks when I'm perfectly calm. Even when I'm not all fired up and pacing the floorboards, when I'm just having a regular, slow, quiet week... I can walk out to that north pasture at sundown, and they are still there. Still telling me what's blessed and what's poisoned. So it's not just the energy, you see? It doesn't matter if I'm flying high or just resting easy, the lines still speak to me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient demonstrates a fixed belief that certain rows of his crops are literally 'blessed' or 'poisoned' based on the voices he hears.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly confirms hearing clear voices coming from the metal irrigation lines when he is out in the pasture.

turns.patient_response:
Well, yes, exactly. That's just what I was trying to explain, Doc. You see, I've really been paying attention to this, because Mary kept insisting it was just me being wound up. I wasn't waking up with that buzzing energy, I wasn't feeling irritable or grand, I was just doing my chores at a regular pace. Eating my meals, sitting on the porch after dinner, sleeping a solid eight hours. Just a quiet, completely normal couple of weeks. 

But even then, during those quiet weeks, if I went down to the north pasture at dusk, I still heard the lines talking. Clear as day. And it wasn't just the voices, either. I'd be sitting at the kitchen table with my ledger, looking over the farm data, the yield reports, and I still knew—I still believed with absolute certainty—that the numbers were carrying hidden warnings about the poisoned rows. Even when my mood was as steady as a rock, those warnings were there, and the voices were there. It doesn't seem to matter if I'm flying high or just having a regular old Tuesday, the truth about the land doesn't change.
